about.title: Personal Injury Help in Huntington Beach, California
about.longDescription: Huntington Beach stretches along Pacific Coast Highway, and on a warm weekend the roads near the pier fill up fast. Beach Boulevard carries much of that traffic inland, and where it meets PCH is one of the highest-volume stretches in the city. Public records for 2025 list 724 injury collisions here, with 1,011 people hurt and 15 lives lost. Collision reports cluster along Route 39 and Route 1, and they tend to peak on Saturday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. If you are one of those numbers, the paperwork can feel heavier than the injury itself. Insurance adjusters call. Bills arrive before you can work again. Questions about fault linger. We're here to help you navigate what comes next. We handle personal injury cases and work on contingency, meaning there is no fee unless there is a recovery. California gives most people two years to file an injury claim, though that window shrinks to as little as six months when a government entity is involved. Reaching out sooner keeps your options open.

whyChoose.title: What California Law Means for Your Huntington Beach Claim

items.title: Two Years, Not Forever
items.desc: Most California injury claims must be filed within two years of the incident. If a city, county, or state agency is involved, you may have only six months to file a claim.

items.title: Partial Fault Doesn't End Your Case
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault. If you were partly responsible, your recovery is reduced by your share, but you are not shut out entirely.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California places no legal cap on non-economic damages such as pain, suffering, and loss of enjoyment of life.

items.title: No Fee Unless There Is a Recovery
items.desc: We work on contingency. You pay nothing upfront, and a fee is only owed if your case results in a recovery.

items.question: Where do crashes in Huntington Beach tend to happen?
items.answer: Public-record collision counts show the highest volumes along Route 39 (Beach Boulevard) and Route 1 (Pacific Coast Highway), the two corridors that carry the most traffic through the city. Reports also peak on Saturdays between 3 p.m. and 5 p.m. These are neutral counts, not a judgment about any particular road; they simply reflect where and when the most vehicles are moving.

items.question: How long do I have to file an injury claim in Huntington Beach?
items.answer: For most personal injury claims in California, the deadline is two years from the date of the injury. If your claim involves a government entity, such as a city vehicle or a public sidewalk, you may need to file a formal claim within six months. We can confirm which deadline applies to your situation.

items.question: Do you provide legal advice?
items.answer: We handle personal injury cases directly. We will review your situation, answer your questions, and represent you in your claim. Our attorneys work on contingency, so there is no upfront cost.

items.question: What if the other driver says I caused the crash?
items.answer: California follows pure comparative fault, so being partly responsible does not bar you from recovering. Your compensation is reduced by your percentage of fault, whatever that turns out to be. Disputed fault is exactly the kind of question we dig into.

items.question: How much does it cost to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: Your initial consultation is free. We work on contingency, meaning no upfront payment and no fee unless there is a recovery in your case. You can ask about the fee percentage before agreeing to anything.
